From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Sara Lin <sara.lin@nimbusretail.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Comm cadence and readiness gap review for API/model cutover

Team —

Following the product meeting last week, Nimbus has asked for a concrete comms cadence and a short list of readiness checks for the planned API/model cutover (we're moving their prod traffic from "embed-v1" to "embed-v2-quant" with the compatibility shim disabled). Sara from Nimbus is on cc. Key asks from Nimbus: a one-page comm timeline they can share with their GTM, a clear exemption signal (what qualifies for an exception lane), and the minimal rollout window we can commit to.

High-level constraints to keep in mind:
- Infra: we need a 72h lead for capacity reservations for Dedicated customers before we toggle region routing.
- CS: we should define risk buckets (high/medium/low) for customers to map to comm lanes.
- Legal/Procure: if customers need SLAs written into amendments, that will add ~14 business days.

Ask: can each of you reply with the following by EOD today?
1) Proposed comm cadence (bullet list of stakeholder-facing notices + expected lead times)
2) Any non-negotiable technical constraints that would block a soft roll (e.g., KV-cache incompatibilities, model kernel gaps)
3) A short definition of what would qualify a customer for an exemption (3 bullets max)

I started a rough comms matrix and put it on Drive (link below). I'll consolidate responses and propose a 2-week pilot cadence.

Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2C3D4-example

Thanks — Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
Product Ops | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Comm cadence and readiness gap review for API/model cutover

Thanks Mateo — quick responses below and attached a first-pass comm cadence spreadsheet (comm_cadence_v1.xlsx).

1) Proposed comm cadence (customer-facing):
- Initial notice (T-30 days): heads up + migration overview + migration FAQ
- Technical bulletin (T-14 days): details about model differences, expected perf/quality changes, and recommended config knobs
- Readiness confirmation (T-7 days): confirm customer test results or request exemption intake
- Cutover reminder (T-48 hours): final checklist + rollback contacts
- Cutover day (T-0): brief status updates and post-cut health check (T+24h)

2) Non-negotiable technical constraints:
- No live traffic on embed-v2-quant unless KV-cache fallback is enabled for customers with >2M tokens/session patterns.
- Region routing must be toggled only after capacity commit is accepted (72h).

3) Exemption criteria (3 buckets):
- High risk: latency-sensitive payments or regulated PII workflows -> require exemption unless customer signs amended SLA
- Medium risk: >50% embedding throughput change in benchmark tests -> recommend canary with RSA monitoring
- Low risk: non-critical analytics workloads -> standard migration lane

Ben and Priyom: can you validate the KV-cache note and confirm whether we can offer a temporary routing shim for Nimbus if they request it?

Attachment: comm_cadence_v1.xlsx

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Ops | Redwood Inference

Folks — tagging onto this thread with technical readiness detail and a proposed minimal timeline. Attached: readiness-gap-log.csv (short list of customers with itemized gaps).

Technical notes / blockers:
- KV-cache: we can enable a per-tenant fallback that emulates previous cache behavior, but it requires toggling a compatibility flag which will double memory usage for the pod during the ramp. We can support that for up to 10 heavy tenants concurrently without impacting cluster SLOs.
- Quantization path: embed-v2-quant has an edge-case where 8-bit attention kernels produce slightly higher variance for sequences >1024 tokens; we recommend internal quality tests for any tenant with >1% long-seq traffic.
- Autoscaling: for Dedicated tenants we need a 72h reservation window as Marissa noted; for Hosted tenants we can do a softer ramp but may see cost spikes if traffic increases quickly.

Proposed minimal timeline (for Nimbus):
- Week 0: T-30 notice + schedule T-10 webinar
- Week 1: Technical bulletin + tenant-level dry run for top 5 tenants (must pass long-seq and perf gates)
- Week 2: Readiness confirmations (T-7) + apply compatibility flag for any exempt tenants
- Cutover week: T-48 reminder -> T-0 toggle -> health check T+24

If Nimbus wants to request an exemption for more than 10 heavy tenants, we need an SLA amendment signed (ProcureOps on cc).

Next step: Sara, can you confirm your top 5 tenants and whether any of them hit the long-seq threshold? I'll sync with Infra to reserve capacity based on that list.

Attachment: readiness-gap-log.csv

—Priyom
